passage: The village school's cricket ground was still green from last week's rain when Siddharth sat on the wall with his notebook. The match against the next village was fixed for Sunday. "What if it rains?" he said aloud to Nitin, who was tying the stumps together. "Then the ground is mud and we have called sixty people for nothing." He tapped his pen. "Plan B. I ask the headmaster for the verandah, carrom and kabaddi indoors, or he keeps next Sunday free for us." Nitin shrugged. "Rain isn't in your hands." "No, but the day can be," said Siddharth. He wrote both options down and walked to the headmaster's office before evening. By the time the sun went down, next Sunday was in the ground register with the school's stamp.

qa.q: Who was tying the stumps together?
qa.a: Nitin was tying the stumps together.
Siddharth worried that the ground would be mud and sixty people would have been called for nothing.

qa.q: What other backup could Siddharth add to his plan?
qa.a: Siddharth could send every player a message about the change by Saturday night, so nobody turns up to a wet ground.

qa.q: How might Nitin see Siddharth's plan B?
qa.a: Nitin might find it fussy at first, since rain is out of anyone's hands, but could come to see that it saves the day.

grounding: Shows a teenager asking what if it rains and arranging an indoor option and a reserved date.

subtype: Approach: asks what if for the main risks and writes a plan B [Thinking]
passage:
Zeynep was in charge of the Year 10 cricket match against the school across town in Nairobi. Two weeks before, she looked at the fixture sheet and asked herself, what if it rains?
The long rains had started early. If the match was washed out, both teams would go home and the season would end without it.
So she wrote Plan B underneath. First, she asked the PE office if the indoor hall was free on the same afternoon. It was, from two to five. An indoor six-a-side game with a tennis ball would do. Second, she asked both coaches to hold the following Saturday as a reserve date.
Her teammate Abebe laughed. "You planned a match that hasn't even been rained on yet."
On the day, it poured at one. By two, both teams were in the hall, playing six-a-side. Nobody went home.

qa.q: When was the indoor hall free?
qa.a: It was free from two to five.

qa.q: What was Zeynep worried about two weeks before the match?
qa.a: She was worried the long rains would wash out the match and the season would end without it being played.

qa.q: What else could Zeynep add to the plan, and why?
qa.a: She could tell both teams about Plan B in advance, so everyone knows where to go if it rains.

qa.q: How might Abebe see Plan B on the day?
qa.a: Abebe, who laughed at first, may be grateful and impressed when the rain comes and nobody has to go home.

grounding: It shows a teenager organising a cricket match asking what if it rains, and arranging an indoor game and a reserve date so the day is not lost.

passage:
In the sports room of the Bhopal girls' school, Afreen pinned the notice for Saturday's inter-house cricket match. Then she stood back and frowned at the sky through the window.
"What if it rains?" she said to Sudha Ma'am, the games teacher. "It's July. If it's washed out, the final gets cancelled and the Class 12 girls never get to play before they leave."
Sudha Ma'am raised her eyebrows. "So what's your plan?"
Afreen took out her notebook. "Plan A: ground at nine. Plan B: if it's raining at eight, we move to the indoor hall and play tennis-ball cricket, six a side. Plan C: if the hall's taken, we use next Saturday. Can you book both?"
Ma'am booked the hall and wrote next Saturday in the register.
It drizzled at eight. By nine, both houses were in the hall, cheering.

qa.q: What is Plan B if it is raining at eight?
qa.a: They move to the indoor hall and play tennis-ball cricket, six a side.
She was worried that rain would cancel the final and the Class 12 girls would never get to play before they leave.

qa.q: What else could Afreen check the day before, and why?
qa.a: She could check the weather forecast and tell both houses on Friday which plan is likely, so no one waits at the ground.

qa.q: How might the Class 12 girls feel about Afreen's plan?
qa.a: They may feel grateful and happy that they still got to play their last match despite the drizzle.

grounding: It shows a teenager organising a cricket match asking what if it rains, and arranging an indoor game and a reserve date with the school.
